assessments.reasoning: MS-VBAL v20250520 PDF page 46 §5.2.1.3 expressly sets explicit-mode when a module contains the directive and implicit-mode otherwise. The nearby static-semantics clauses confirm its placement in procedural or class modules.

challenge.method: Compared the present and absent cases, class and procedural modules, and a possible interpretation that the directive fixes variable types. Compared the product reference's Deftype case (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/option-explicit-statement) and the same PDF's distinct declaration-mode and implicit-declaration sections.
challenge.results: The standard selects declaration mode. VBA type-default rules can still affect undeclared variables where implicit declarations are allowed, and an editor can generate source without changing the rule for a module that omits the directive. These readings leave the stated mode rule intact.

limitations: The reviewed normative claim describes the module's mode. It does not establish editor defaults or the outcome of a specific program's declaration or type inference.
